newsitem.title: UK: Robert Fleming reports 16 pct H1 pretax profit rise.
newsitem.headline: Robert Fleming reports 16 pct H1 pretax profit rise.

text.p: Privately-owned British investment banking group Robert Fleming said on Wednesday its pretax profit for the first half of the year had increased by 16 percent to 92.2 million pounds ($153.9 million).

Flemings also announced an increased interim dividend of 8.0 pence per share, from 7.0 pence. John Manser, its chief executive, said that while the outlook for the year was promising, the firm would have to contend with flat Asian markets and heightened competitive pressures in other markets. ($1=.5990 Pound)
Robert Fleming reports 16 pct H1 pretax profit rise

Flemings said in a statement that it had seen strong profit growth from its fund management businesses and its securities business had reported "a marked increase in profits aided by a strong performance by UK and continental European broking".

The group said its Jardine Fleming joint venture with Jardine Matheson Holdings Ltd recorded a "marginally lower" interim result than its net interim profit of $63.9 million in 1995 after taking into account provisions "arising from the regulatory issues of earlier years".
Flemings said its capital markets arm had helped companies raise 13.4 billion pounds of new capital while its corporate finance division had completed 43 deals during the period.

It also announced that Robin Fleming will retire as chairman of Robert Fleming Holdings at the end of March 1997 and John Manser will replace him. William Garrett will become chief executive and chairman of the group executive committee.
